title: Plan paths in one canonical form

ground.note: ExtractedPhaseFields: the three file lists are bare Schema.Array(Schema.String), shared by the extracted plan, the persisted phax-plan.json and (through answerPhaseFields) the extraction answer.
PlanDocumentPhaseSchema reuses ExtractedPhaseFields' file lists; a headless planner's answer and a plan's JSON sidecar decode through it.
PlanExtractionAnswerSchema: the extraction model's answer, phases built from answerPhaseFields.
The deterministic plan.md reader: list items taken as written, the candidate decoded through ExtractedPhaxPlanSchema; a structure error makes the caller fall back to the extraction model.
Planned paths matched against the run's diff by string equality.
filePlanFindings and plannedPaths: create/edit collision, already-created and working-tree probe, all on the string as written.
Assignment bounds govern a phase through matchesAnyGlob over its three lists.
Its own normaliseRepoRelative: today the one reader that normalizes, silently skipping absolute and `..` paths.
planInputFromPhaxPlan feeds the overlap footprints straight from the plan's lists.
The plan's footprint (buildFootprint) is compared with what git says changed since approval.
posix.normalize already used in the domain to tell a path that leaves the repository.
readPhaxPlanFile: a phax-plan.json stamped below the current stamp is read by a frozen decoder, displayed, never handed to a run; older plan sidecars are lifted, and a lift can be refused.
migrate-documents refuses a plan whose lift is refused, naming the phase and the departing value.
Current stamps: phax-plan, plan-document and phax-plan-extraction at 0.33.0; PHAX_RELEASE 0.38.0, not yet cut.

context:
A plan phase names its files in three lists: `plannedFilesToCreate`, `plannedFilesToEdit` and `optionalFilesToEdit`. They reach phax by three routes. The first is the deterministic reading of a plan.md's `### Planned files to create`, `### Planned files to edit` and `### Optional files that may be edited` sections. The second is the extraction model's answer, used when that reading fails. The third is the plan document, which is both a headless planner's answer and a plan's JSON sidecar. All three end in the persisted `phax-plan.json`. Every route decodes the lists as plain strings (`Schema.Array(Schema.String)`), so `./src/widget.ts`, `src//widget.ts` and `src/a/../widget.ts` decode as written, and none of them equals the `src/widget.ts` that git reports.

Several readers compare those strings as written: reconciliation (planned paths against the run's diff), plan lint (create/edit collision, "already created by", the working-tree probe), assignment bounds (globs over the three lists), `phax plans overlap` (plan footprints), and plan staleness (the footprint against git's changes since approval). Only the skill-edit grant normalizes, with its own private helper.

Pull request #205 normalized inside the overlap footprints only. It was declined: every other reader would still compare raw strings and disagree with the overlap report. On 2026-11-13 the operator gave the direction: one schema for a plan path, shared by the three lists on every route; canonical means repository-relative, `/` separators, no `.`, empty or `..` segment, and no leading or trailing `/`; and readers do no normalizing of their own.
problem: The same file can be written several ways, and phax treats each spelling as a different file. A phase that plans `./src/x.ts` and changes `src/x.ts` gets two deviations: one missing file and one unplanned file. Two plans that edit the same file under two spellings are reported as clean by `phax plans overlap`. Lint does not see a create/edit collision. The model-assignment bound for `src/**` does not apply to the phase. Staleness misses a change to a file the plan touches. A path that leaves the repository (`../x.ts`) or is absolute (`/src/x.ts`) decodes without complaint and simply never matches anything. Fixing this in one reader, as #205 did, makes the readers disagree with each other. Any reader added later would also have to remember to normalize.

productGoal.statement: Every plan path reaches phax's readers in one canonical, repository-relative form. phax decides that form once, when it decodes the plan, so every check compares the same strings that git reports. A path with no canonical form is refused at that point, with a message naming the phase and the path. Plans whose paths are already canonical behave exactly as before.
productGoal.guidingRule: A plan path is made canonical, or refused, where the plan is decoded, and nowhere else.

terminology.definition: One entry of a phase's `plannedFilesToCreate`, `plannedFilesToEdit` or `optionalFilesToEdit`. It names a file.
A plan path exactly as it appears in its source: a plan.md list item (backticks unwrapped, as today), an extraction answer, or a plan document.
A non-empty path relative to the repository root, using `/` as the separator. It has no empty segment, no `.` segment and no `..` segment, and no leading or trailing `/`. Example: `src/widget.ts`.
The path obtained by dropping empty and `.` segments and resolving each `..` against the segment before it. `./src/x.ts`, `src//x.ts` and `src/a/../x.ts` all have the canonical form `src/x.ts`.

A written path that has no canonical form. This covers five cases: it is empty, or its canonical form is empty (`.`, `./`, `a/..`); it starts with `/` (absolute); its `..` segments climb above the repository root (it leaves the repository); it ends with `/` (it names a directory); or it contains `\` (a backslash, which phax will not read as a separator).
A check that compares plan paths: reconciliation, plan lint's file checks, assignment bounds, `phax plans overlap`, plan staleness and the skill-edit grant.

requirements.title: Only canonical paths are held
requirements.statement: The system shall hold only canonical paths in every phase file list it decodes, persists to `phax-plan.json` or a plan document, or hands to a reader.

requirements.title: Unplannable paths are refused
requirements.statement: IF a written path is unplannable THEN the system SHALL refuse the plan with a message naming the phase, the list, the written path and why it is unplannable.

requirements.title: No model fallback for an unplannable path
requirements.statement: IF the deterministic reading of a plan.md meets an unplannable path THEN the system SHALL refuse the plan with that path's refusal, without falling back to the extraction model.

requirements.title: Reading a plan.md rewrites to canonical form
requirements.statement: WHEN phax reads a plan from a plan.md, deterministically or through the extraction model's answer, and a written path is plannable but not canonical, THE system SHALL replace it with its canonical form.

requirements.title: The plan document refuses a non-canonical path
requirements.statement: IF a plan document (a headless planner's answer or a plan's JSON sidecar) holds a plannable path that is not canonical THEN the system SHALL refuse it with a message naming the phase, the list, the written path and its canonical form.

requirements.title: Readers treat spellings of one file alike
requirements.statement: The system shall report the same reconciliation, lint, assignment-bound, overlap and staleness results for a plan whose plan.md writes a path in a non-canonical form as for the same plan written with that path's canonical form.

requirements.title: Canonical plans are unchanged
requirements.statement: The system shall give a plan whose paths are all canonical the same behaviour and the same output as before this change, apart from the `$schema` stamps of the documents it writes.

requirements.title: An earlier-shape phax-plan.json is never run
requirements.statement: IF a run is resumed from a `phax-plan.json` stamped at a shape before this change THEN the system SHALL refuse it as it refuses any earlier-shape phax-plan, while still reading it for display with its paths as written.

requirements.title: An earlier-shape sidecar with a non-canonical path is not migrated
requirements.statement: IF `phax artifact migrate-documents` meets a plan sidecar stamped at an earlier shape that holds a plan path that is not canonical THEN the system SHALL refuse to migrate that plan, naming the phase, the list and the path, and leave its files unchanged.

requirements.title: The published schemas state the rule
requirements.statement: The system shall describe the canonical-path rule on each of the three file lists in the published plan-document and phax-plan JSON Schemas.

surface.summary: A plan document, whether a headless planner's answer or a sidecar, is refused when a file list holds a path that is not canonical, and the refusal names the spelling to write instead.
surface.after:
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/plan-document/0.38.0.json",
  "phases": [{ "id": "phase-02",
    "plannedFilesToEdit": ["./src/x.ts", "../shared/y.ts"], … }]
}
# refused at the first violation:
phases[1].plannedFilesToEdit[0]: phase-02 plans "./src/x.ts", which is not canonical: write "src/x.ts"
# with plannedFilesToEdit ["src/x.ts", "../shared/y.ts"]:
phases[1].plannedFilesToEdit[1]: phase-02 plans "../shared/y.ts", which leaves the repository

surface.summary: Lint reads `./src/x.ts` in a plan.md as `src/x.ts`, names files by that spelling in its findings, and reports an unplannable path as an error on its phase.
surface.before:
$ phax plans lint docs/plans/2611140900-widget-plan.md
# phase-01 create: ./src/x.ts   edit: src/x.ts   → no finding
surface.after:
$ phax plans lint docs/plans/2611140900-widget-plan.md
✗ phase-01 files: create and edit both list src/x.ts

# a plan.md listing `../shared/y.ts` under Planned files to edit:
✗ phase-02: Planned files to edit: "../shared/y.ts" leaves the repository
$? = 1

surface.summary: Two plans that write the same file under two spellings are reported as overlapping on that file's canonical path.
surface.before:
$ phax plans overlap plan-a.md plan-b.md
no shared files
surface.after:
$ phax plans overlap plan-a.md plan-b.md
shared: src/x.ts  (plan-a edit, plan-b edit)

surface.summary: A phase that plans `./src/x.ts` and changes `src/x.ts` is reconciled as having edited a planned file, with no missing or unplanned entry.
surface.before:
Missing planned edits:
  ./src/x.ts
Unplanned edits:
  src/x.ts

surface.summary: An older plan sidecar holding a path that is not canonical is refused by name, so the operator can fix the path and re-approve.
surface.after:
$ phax artifact migrate-documents
✗ docs/plans/2610020800-widget-plan.md phase-02 plannedFilesToEdit "./src/x.ts" is not canonical: write "src/x.ts"
  edit the path in the plan, then re-approve it

surface.summary: A run's phax-plan.json holds only canonical paths and is stamped with the release that introduced the rule.
phax code decodes every plan file list through one plan-path schema, so a reader can rely on canonical strings and never normalizes them itself.
surface.before:
plannedFilesToCreate: Schema.Array(Schema.String)
plannedFilesToEdit:   Schema.Array(Schema.String)
optionalFilesToEdit:  Schema.Array(Schema.String)

nonGoals: Symbolic links: a path through a symlinked directory is not resolved to its target.
Case-only differences (`Src/x.ts` vs `src/x.ts`) and Unicode normalization of file names.
Globs in plans: the file lists name files, and a glob character is not given any meaning.
Normalizing paths that come from git, which are canonical already.
A lint finding that a plan.md writes a non-canonical spelling which phax rewrote.
Planning a file whose name contains a backslash.
Lifting an earlier-shape phax-plan.json so an in-flight run can continue across the upgrade.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Reconciliation matches a non-canonical planned path
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan.md whose phase-01 lists `./src/x.ts` under Planned files to edit, and a phase session that modifies `src/x.ts` and nothing else
acceptanceCriteria.then: `src/x.ts` is reported as edited as planned, with no missing planned edit, no unplanned edit and no deviation. The report is identical to the one for the same plan written with `src/x.ts`.

acceptanceCriteria.name: Lint sees a create/edit collision across spellings
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan.md whose phase-01 lists `./src/x.ts` under Planned files to create and `src/x.ts` under Planned files to edit
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reports the error `create and edit both list src/x.ts` on phase-01

acceptanceCriteria.name: Lint sees a file already created under another spelling
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan.md where phase-01 creates `src//x.ts` and phase-02 creates `src/x.ts`, and `src/x.ts` is absent from the working tree
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reports `create src/x.ts: already created by phase-01` on phase-02

acceptanceCriteria.name: Lint's working-tree probe finds a non-canonical path
acceptanceCriteria.given: a working tree holding `src/x.ts` and a plan.md whose phase-01 lists `./src/x.ts` under Planned files to edit
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reports no `does not exist` error for that path

acceptanceCriteria.name: Assignment bounds govern a non-canonical path
acceptanceCriteria.given: an assignment bound governing `src/**` and a plan.md whose phase-01 lists only `./src/x.ts` and has a model outside the bound with no assignment reason
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reports the `outside` error naming that bound on phase-01, as it does for the same plan written with `src/x.ts`

acceptanceCriteria.name: Overlap sees one file under two spellings
acceptanceCriteria.given: plan A whose plan.md edits `./src/x.ts` and plan B whose plan.md edits `src/x.ts`
acceptanceCriteria.then: it reports both plans as sharing `src/x.ts`

acceptanceCriteria.name: Staleness sees a change to a non-canonical planned file
acceptanceCriteria.given: an approved plan whose plan.md edits `./src/x.ts`, and a commit since its approval that changes `src/x.ts`
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax plans status` reports on the plan
acceptanceCriteria.then: its staleness verdict is the one it gives the same plan written with `src/x.ts`

acceptanceCriteria.name: phax-plan.json holds the canonical form
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan.md listing `./src/x.ts`, `src//y.ts` and `src/a/../z.ts`, read both deterministically and through an extraction answer that writes those spellings
acceptanceCriteria.then: the run's `phax-plan.json` lists `src/x.ts`, `src/y.ts` and `src/z.ts` and is stamped `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/phax-plan/0.38.0.json`

acceptanceCriteria.name: Each kind of unplannable path is refused
acceptanceCriteria.given: for each of `""`, `./`, `/src/x.ts`, `../x.ts`, `src/../../x.ts`, `src/` and `src\x.ts`, a plan document whose phase-02 lists it under plannedFilesToEdit, and a plan.md whose phase-02 lists it under Planned files to edit
acceptanceCriteria.when: the plan document is decoded, and `phax plans lint` runs on the plan.md
acceptanceCriteria.then: each is refused with a message naming phase-02, the list, the written path and its reason (empty, absolute, leaves the repository, names a directory, or backslash)

acceptanceCriteria.name: An unplannable path in plan.md never reaches the model
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan.md otherwise well formed whose phase-02 lists `../x.ts`, with a stub extraction backend that records calls
acceptanceCriteria.then: the plan is refused naming phase-02 and `../x.ts`, and the backend records no call

acceptanceCriteria.name: A plan document with a non-canonical path is refused
acceptanceCriteria.given: a headless planner answer whose phase-02 lists `./src/x.ts` under plannedFilesToEdit
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is refused with `phases[1].plannedFilesToEdit[0]` naming phase-02, `./src/x.ts` and the canonical form `src/x.ts`, and no plan file is written

acceptanceCriteria.name: A canonical plan is unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.given: the repository's existing canonical plans and the hello-world example plan
acceptanceCriteria.when: `phax plans lint`, `phax plans overlap` and `phax plans status` run on them before and after the change

acceptanceCriteria.name: An earlier-shape phax-plan.json is displayed, never run
acceptanceCriteria.when: phax displays its run, and then a resume of that run is attempted
acceptanceCriteria.then: the display shows `./src/x.ts` as written, and the resume is refused as for any earlier-shape plan

acceptanceCriteria.name: An earlier-shape sidecar with a non-canonical path is not migrated
acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan sidecar stamped `https://docs.phax.run/schemas/plan-document/0.33.0.json` whose phase-02 lists `./src/x.ts`
acceptanceCriteria.then: that plan is refused, with a message naming phase-02, plannedFilesToEdit and `./src/x.ts`, and its .md and .json are unchanged

acceptanceCriteria.name: The published schema states the rule
acceptanceCriteria.then: each of the three file lists' items carries the canonical-path rule in its JSON Schema

openQuestions.question: A path that is not canonical but has a canonical form (`./src/x.ts`, `src//x.ts`, `src/a/../x.ts`): should the decode rewrite it or refuse it, and on which route?

options.label: Rewrite when phax reads a plan.md (the deterministic reading and the extraction answer); refuse in the plan document
options.abandons: Exact correspondence between a hand-written plan.md and phax-plan.json: the plan.md keeps `./src/x.ts` while every report says `src/x.ts`.

options.label: Refuse on every route
options.abandons: Tolerance of harmless variation: a model's or an author's `./` fails extraction, and the operator must edit a plan.md and re-approve it over a cosmetic spelling.

options.label: Rewrite on every route, the plan document included
options.abandons: The plan document as written and approved: phax would hold different paths from the sidecar's bytes, and any rewrite of the sidecar (decide, migrate) would silently change approved content.

openQuestions.rationale: phax-plan.json is a projection of a plan.md and never a byte-for-byte copy, so rewriting while reading a plan.md loses nothing that was approved. It also keeps a model's harmless `./` from failing an extraction. The plan document is the artifact itself, written by a planner and approved by an operator, so it should hold exactly what phax reads; a refusal that names the canonical spelling costs the planner one retry.

settled: One plan-path schema is used by all three file lists on every route: plan.md reading, extraction answer, plan document, phax-plan.json and the extracted-plan cache.
The meanings of canonical and unplannable are as defined in §4. Unplannable paths are refused on every route.
Readers are not changed to normalize. The skill-edit grant's private normalizer becomes redundant and may be removed, provided its output is unchanged.

The phax-plan, plan-document and phax-plan-extraction formats each move to the stamp of the next release cut (currently 0.38.0), each with a frozen 0.33.0 decoder, following the existing persisted.ts pattern.
No back-compat shim: an earlier-shape sidecar holding a path that is not canonical is a refused lift, not rewritten.
open: If q-rewrite is decided as refuse-everywhere, the per-reader criteria are restated with the plan written as `src/x.ts`, and ac-unplannable is extended to cover non-canonical spellings. If it is decided as rewrite-everywhere, ac-document-refuses is dropped.

The exact refusal wording. The content is normative: the phase, the list (its field name in JSON and its section title in plan.md), the written path, the reason, and the canonical form where one exists.
How the extracted-plan cache drops entries written before the change, for example by bumping the extractor version.
constraints: Changes are additive for canonical plans: no change in output apart from `$schema` stamps.
The canonical-path rule is pure domain logic with no filesystem access. It never consults the working tree to decide a path's form.

The extraction answer's JSON Schema, which the model is shown, must still admit a plannable non-canonical path if q-rewrite is decided as rewrite-reading, so that the model's `./` is rewritten rather than refused.
The two tests from pull request #205 (overlap across spellings) should pass unchanged against the decoded plan, not against a normalizing footprint.

docsPage.why: There is no user docs page for plan file lists. The rule appears in the published plan-document schema (`phax artifact schema plan`) and in refusal messages; the planner may add one line to the phax-planning skill.
